evidence_gaps:
  - >-
    Almost every camel milk value in the library is for raw milk; a few are for
    shubat (fermented camel milk) or for milk boiled in one study. The library
    holds no metal values for pasteurized camel milk, camel milk powder, camel
    milk cheese or chal.
  - >-
    Measured regions are Pakistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia,
    Xinjiang in China and Nigeria. No values are verified for the United Arab
    Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Mongolia, Somalia, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan,
    India or Algeria.
  - >-
    Several camel milk studies are small or lack quality checks, and printed
    tables sometimes disagree with the same paper's text. Those values are kept
    as printed and flagged on their rows.
  - >-
    Yang et al. 2025 state no quality-control data for their Tacheng samples,
    and the Tacheng camel milk values for beryllium, cobalt, cadmium, vanadium
    and antimony are about 20 to 60 times those from Altay and Ili; treat the
    Tacheng values as unreviewed.
  - >-
    Soryal et al. 2026 is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and its
    table of detection limits does not line up with its own results.
  - >-
    Abdelrahman et al. 2025 print different lead means for the same samples in
    Table 5 and Table 6; both are shown as printed. Their quality check used a
    water reference material, not a milk one.
  - >-
    Mostafidi et al. 2016 report a chromium value for Qazvin although their
    conclusion says no chromium was found; Shar et al. 2021 print cadmium and
    lead values below their own stated detection limit; Batool et al. 2019
    report lead of 0.667 to 3.17 ppm from one sample per milk type without a
    detection limit.

# Camel milk

Camel milk in the HMI library has 550 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ag, B, Ba, Be, Bi, Ca, K, <ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel and chromium and others, in 550 results from 16 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abdelrahman MM, Alobre MM, Qaid MM, Al-Badwi MA, Matar AM, Aboragah AA, Amran RA, Aljumaah RS · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Regional and Seasonal Dynamics of Heavy Metal Accumulation in Saudi Dromedary Camel Serum and Milk as Bioindicators of Environmental Quality</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Sustainability 2025, 17, 10205</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahmad I, Zaman A, Samad N, Ayaz MM, Rukh S, Akbar A, Ullah N · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals">Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometery Detection of Heavy Metals in Milk of Camel, Cattle, Buffalo and Goat from Various Areas of Khyber- Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), Pakistan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Analytical &amp; </li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Camel milk, as sold from raw camel milk samples from which E. coli was isolated had cadmium higher at 3.2 µg/kg, against 3.1 µg/kg for raw camel milk samples from which S. aureus was isolated in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yazdanian Ghahfarokhi E, Shakerian A, Sharafati Chaleshtori R, Rahimi E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Investigation of the abundance of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (including virulence gene profiles) and heavy metal contamination in camel milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Medicine and Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abdelrahman MM, Alobre MM, Qaid MM, Al-Badwi MA, Matar AM, Aboragah AA, Amran RA, Aljumaah RS · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Regional and Seasonal Dynamics of Heavy Metal Accumulation in Saudi Dromedary Camel Serum and Milk as Bioindicators of Environmental Quality</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Sustainability 2025, 17, 10205</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahmad I, Zaman A, Samad N, Ayaz MM, Rukh S, Akbar A, Ullah N · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals">Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometery Detection of Heavy Metals in Milk of Camel, Cattle, Buffalo and Goat from Various Areas of Khyber- Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), Pakistan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Analytical &amp; Bioanalytical Techniques 2017, 8(3): 367</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Batool T, Mahmood Z, Riaz M, Dogar MZH, Irshad S, Murtaza MA, Mehmood K, Rasool G, Irshad A, Sadia H · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals">Comparative study of nutritional status, minerals and heavy metal contents in tetra pack branded milk samples with fresh milk from selected milk producing animals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Biosciences 15(1):162-168</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chen L, Li X, Li Z, Deng L · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china">Analysis of 17 elements in cow, goat, buffalo, yak, and camel milk by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">RSC Advances</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the camel milk came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

Almost every camel milk value in the library is for raw milk; a few are for shubat (fermented camel milk) or for milk boiled in one study. The library holds no metal values for pasteurized camel milk, camel milk powder, camel milk cheese or chal. Measured regions are Pakistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Xinjiang in China and Nigeria. No values are verified for the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Mongolia, Somalia, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, India or Algeria. Several camel milk studies are small or lack quality checks, and printed tables sometimes disagree with the same paper's text. Those values are kept as printed and flagged on their rows. Yang et al. 2025 state no quality-control data for their Tacheng samples, and the Tacheng camel milk values for beryllium, cobalt, cadmium, vanadium and antimony are about 20 to 60 times those from Altay and Ili; treat the Tacheng values as unreviewed. Soryal et al. 2026 is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and its table of detection limits does not line up with its own results. Abdelrahman et al. 2025 print different lead means for the same samples in Table 5 and Table 6; both are shown as printed. Their quality check used a water reference material, not a milk one. Mostafidi et al. 2016 report a chromium value for Qazvin although their conclusion says no chromium was found; Shar et al. 2021 print cadmium and lead values below their own stated detection limit; Batool et al. 2019 report lead of 0.667 to 3.17 ppm from one sample per milk type without a detection limit.

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of camel milk, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach camel milk

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach camel milk comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Camel milk, as sold from raw camel milk samples from which E. coli was isolated had cadmium higher at 3.2 µg/kg, against 3.1 µg/kg for raw camel milk samples from which S. aureus was isolated in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yazdanian Ghahfarokhi E, Shakerian A, Sharafati Chaleshtori R, Rahimi E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Investigation of the abundance of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (including virulence gene profiles) and heavy metal contamination in camel milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Medicine and Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

In one study, lead across 8 groups of camel milk ranged from 10 µg/kg (Zhambyl oblast, Kazakhstan) to 60 µg/kg (Almaty oblast, Kazakhstan); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Konuspayeva G, Jurjanz S, Loiseau G, Barci V, Akhmetsadykova S, Meldebekova AA, Faye B · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants">Contamination of Camel Milk (Heavy Metals, Organic Pollutants and Radionuclides) in Kazakhstan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Protection, 2011, 2, 90-96</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 8 groups of camel milk ranged from 0.92 µg/kg (animals aged ≤2 years) to 14.4 µg/kg (animals aged 5 years or older); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Parsaei P, Rahimi E, Shakerian A · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury">Concentrations of Cadmium, Lead and Mercury in Raw Bovine, Ovine, Caprine, Buffalo and Camel Milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for camel milk

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yazdanian Ghahfarokhi E, Shakerian A, Sharafati Chaleshtori R, Rahimi E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Investigation of the abundance of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (including virulence gene profiles) and heavy metal contamination in camel milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Medicine and Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Camel milk FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-camel-milk" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-camel-milk" data-question="What heavy metals are found in camel milk?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in camel milk?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ag, B, Ba, Be, Bi, Ca, K, Li, Mg, Mo, Na, Si, Sr, Ti and Tl in camel milk, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abdelrahman MM, Alobre MM, Qaid MM, Al-Badwi MA, Matar AM, Aboragah AA, Amran RA, Aljumaah RS · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Regional and Seasonal Dynamics of Heavy Metal Accumulation in Saudi Dromedary Camel Serum and Milk as Bioindicators of Environmental Quality</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Sustainability 2025, 17, 10205</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdelrahman2025-saudi-camel-milk-serum-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahmad I, Zaman A, Samad N, Ayaz MM, Rukh S, Akbar A, Ullah N · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals">Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometery Detection of Heavy Metals in Milk of Camel, Cattle, Buffalo and Goat from Various Areas of Khyber- Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), Pakistan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Analytical &amp; Bioanalytical Techniques 2017, 8(3): 367</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ahmad2017-kpk-camel-cattle-buffalo-goat-milk-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Batool T, Mahmood Z, Riaz M, Dogar MZH, Irshad S, Murtaza MA, Mehmood K, Rasool G, Irshad A, Sadia H · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals">Comparative study of nutritional status, minerals and heavy metal contents in tetra pack branded milk samples with fresh milk from selected milk producing animals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Biosciences 15(1):162-168</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/batool2019-pakistan-camel-cow-milk-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chen L, Li X, Li Z, Deng L · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china">Analysis of 17 elements in cow, goat, buffalo, yak, and camel milk by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">RSC Advances</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chen2020-milk-types-elements-china">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-camel-milk" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-camel-milk" data-question="How do heavy metals get into camel milk?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into camel milk?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, camel milk from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than camel milk from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yazdanian Ghahfarokhi E, Shakerian A, Sharafati Chaleshtori R, Rahimi E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Investigation of the abundance of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (including virulence gene profiles) and heavy metal contamination in camel milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Medicine and Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Camel milk, as sold from raw camel milk samples from which E. coli was isolated had cadmium higher at 3.2 µg/kg, against 3.1 µg/kg for raw camel milk samples from which S. aureus was isolated in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yazdanian Ghahfarokhi E, Shakerian A, Sharafati Chaleshtori R, Rahimi E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Investigation of the abundance of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (including virulence gene profiles) and heavy metal contamination in camel milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Medicine and Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yazdanian2025-camel-milk-heavy-metals-iran">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-camel-milk-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-camel-milk-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of camel milk measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of camel milk measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 8 groups of camel milk ranged from 10 µg/kg (Zhambyl oblast, Kazakhstan) to 60 µg/kg (Almaty oblast, Kazakhstan); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Konuspayeva G, Jurjanz S, Loiseau G, Barci V, Akhmetsadykova S, Meldebekova AA, Faye B · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants">Contamination of Camel Milk (Heavy Metals, Organic Pollutants and Radionuclides) in Kazakhstan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Protection, 2011, 2, 90-96</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/konuspayeva2011-kazakhstan-camel-milk-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 8 groups of camel milk ranged from 0.92 µg/kg (animals aged ≤2 years) to 14.4 µg/kg (animals aged 5 years or older); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Parsaei P, Rahimi E, Shakerian A · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury">Concentrations of Cadmium, Lead and Mercury in Raw Bovine, Ovine, Caprine, Buffalo and Camel Milk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/parsaei2019-milk-cadmium-lead-mercury">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
